title: Geo & Cartography — Where It Stands
thesis: A genuine standout: 44 self-inverting projections, full WGS84 geodesy, and a spatstat-class spatial-statistics engine ship together behind Ring faces, guarded by ~400 assertions and 72 negative controls. It is the rare library where the tool that draws the map also computes the statistics it shows and measures its own distortion — analysis-and-cartography strong, GIS-plumbing light.

lanes.note: 44 projections across five families, all with inverses; a shared 2D Newton solver refuses any inverse not round-tripping to 1e-6; rotate/clip/fit, UTM
WGS84 + ellipsoid table, geodesic inverse/direct, rhumb lines, ECEF/ENU, DMS, meridian arc, polygon area on the ellipsoid with geodesic edges
Clark-Evans z-test, Ripley K/L/G/F with Monte-Carlo envelopes, IDW, variograms, ordinary kriging with variance surface, 7+ point-process null models
lanes.proof: geo_stats.zig / geo_interp.zig / geo_process.zig; kriging-variance invariance guard

lanes.note: Choropleth (equal-area default), proportional symbol, flow (great circles), hex-bin, bloc/membership, insets with a measured locator scale
Graticule, Tissot indicatrix on the same Jacobian, a scale bar that refuses to lie, north arrow, day-night terminator, even-spaced streamlines
stzGeoFeatures reads GeoJSON and TopoJSON with an engine-side filtered read (a 40 MB file yields only wanted features); read-only, no writer
stzGeoAtlas binds name->shape without vendoring data; the Niger real-data map (geoBoundaries ADM1 + RGPH-2012) is the cap; no fuzzy name matching
Ring area (planar/spherical/ellipsoidal), centroid, point-in-polygon, bounding boxes, spatial join; no buffer/intersection/union/convex hull
Projections are a display transform (lon/lat in, pixels out); no source-CRS reprojection from UTM or a national grid
Scalar density fields, an ESRI ASCII grid reader, per-pixel resampled field image, marching-squares contours; no hillshade/slope/aspect, no GeoTIFF
Maps emit interactive SVG with per-region ids, classes and <title> hooks (SetInteractive, GE2c); no live pan/zoom, by plan the GUI plane's job
None: no slippy-tile scheme, no tile server, no web-map basemap integration anywhere in the geo module

standouts: 44 self-inverting projections with a solver that refuses a bad inverse
the tool that draws the map also computes the statistics and measures its own distortion
ordinary kriging with its variance surface
the Niger real-data map, vendor-free end to end
